idea.title: 5 moments agents lose buyers
idea.angle: Enquiry, after viewing, price question, weekend, late night: where leads leak
idea.hook: Most buyers aren't lost in the negotiation. They're lost in five quiet moments.

slides.heading: 5 quiet moments where agents **lose buyers**
slides.body: Not in the negotiation. Much earlier.

slides.heading: The **first enquiry**
slides.body: A buyer DMs 'Is the East Legon flat still available?' You're on a viewing. By the time you reply, they've asked three other agents.

slides.heading: Right **after the viewing**
slides.body: They liked the house. You drove off and moved to the next client. No message that evening, so the excitement fades.

slides.heading: The **price question**
slides.body: 'How much?' gets a slow or vague answer. Buyers read silence as 'too expensive' and quietly move on.

slides.heading: The **weekend**
slides.body: Saturday is when buyers in Lekki and Kumasi finally have time to browse. If your phone is off till Monday, so is your pipeline.

slides.heading: **Late** at night
slides.body: A diaspora buyer in London messages at 11pm your time. Nobody answers until morning. By then they've found someone who did.

slides.heading: Plug the leaks
bullets: Reply to every enquiry within minutes
Message every buyer the evening of a viewing
Have a clear price answer ready to send
Decide who covers weekends and late nights

caption:
Most buyers aren't lost in the negotiation. They're lost in five quiet moments.

1. The first enquiry that waits too long
2. The evening after a viewing with no message
3. The price question that gets a vague answer
4. The weekend when your phone is off
5. The late-night DM nobody sees till morning

None of these need more leads to fix. They need a reply at the right time.

idea.title: 4 questions to ask before booking a viewing
idea.angle: Qualify budget, location, timeline and decision-maker so viewings aren't wasted
idea.hook: A wasted viewing costs you a morning. Four questions prevent most of them.

slides.heading: 4 questions to ask **before** you book a viewing
A viewing is **not free**
slides.body: Fuel, Accra traffic, a lost morning. If the buyer can't afford it or isn't ready, that time is gone. A few questions first protect it.

slides.heading: Ask about **budget**
slides.body: Send: 'So I show you the right options, what budget range are you working with?' Then match listings to the answer, not the hope.

slides.heading: Ask about **location**
slides.body: Send: 'Which areas work for you, and is there anywhere you'd rather avoid?' Lekki Phase 1 and Ajah are very different conversations.

slides.heading: Ask about **timing**
slides.body: Send: 'When are you hoping to move in?' Next month and next year are both fine. They just need different follow-up.

slides.heading: Ask who **decides**
slides.body: Send: 'Will anyone else be part of the decision? Happy to have them at the viewing too.' Saves a second trip for the spouse.

slides.heading: AI only qualifies well when someone teaches it **the right questions.**
slides.body: A Kortexa principle

caption:
A wasted viewing costs you a morning. Four questions prevent most of them.

Budget: so you only show what they can buy.
Location: so you don't drive across town for nothing.
Timeline: so you know how hard to follow up.
Decision-maker: so the real buyer is in the room.

The same goes for any chatbot answering your DMs. It only qualifies well if the right questions are built into it.

idea.title: What to send after a viewing
idea.angle: A same-day follow-up that moves the buyer to the next step
idea.hook: The viewing went well. What you send that evening decides what happens next.

slides.heading: What to send **after a viewing**
slides.body: Same day. Word for word.

slides.heading: They're seeing **other houses**
slides.body: Most buyers view several places in one weekend. The agent who follows up first, while the house is fresh in their mind, gets the next step.

slides.heading: The **thank-you**
slides.body: 'Thanks for coming to see the house in Tema today. What did you like most, and was anything not quite right for you?'

slides.heading: Make the **next step** easy
slides.body: 'Glad it felt right. Want me to check with the landlord on terms, or book a second look with your partner this week?'

slides.heading: Ask, **don't push**
slides.body: 'No problem at all. If this one isn't it, tell me what to change and I'll send two options that fit better.'

slides.heading: Day 3 **nudge**
slides.body: 'Hi, just checking in on the Tema house. Should I keep it on your list, or start looking for something that fits better?'

slides.heading: Follow-up **rules**
bullets: Never invent pressure or fake interest
Always offer a clear next step

caption:
The viewing went well. What you send that evening decides what happens next.

Send a thank-you within 2 hours and ask what they liked.
If they loved it, offer one easy next step.
If they're unsure, ask what to change and send better options.
If they go quiet, nudge on day 3.

Swap in your own area and property. No fake pressure, just clear next steps.
